LESSON: READING 13.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.2: Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do you read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure
2. use comprehension strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 13.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 13.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure

What this means
In this part you learn to read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use comprehension strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information

What this means
In this part you learn to use comprehension strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use comprehension strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use comprehension strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading to a partner. (skill: use comprehension strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure.
3. Practise this skill: use comprehension strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do you read?
2. What materials do you enjoy reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure.
5. Be able to: use comprehension strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
